svg.aria-label: Six questions to one model: what is given, what is wanted, how each is answered, and whether it exists or is to be trained
svg.text: one pass per 0.2 s block, fifteen blocks: the model as it is (head 1)
P is an output slot of the network, not a search
the property slots read the recording and the action through attention
and are filled in: samples with flow matching (a spread where the recording
does not decide), or one value with a squared error; same slot, other loss
the collapsed bridge: what happened, and what did it
properties known; the action token and the fifteen chunks are generated
together, so each sample is one story that starts at s₀ and ends at sᴛ;
forty samples are the set of causes the end allows; with the action given
as well, only the motion between the ends comes out
today no property is ever hidden in training
some or all property tokens hidden at random during training, so the
motion is predicted from the properties seen for such objects, and the hidden
ones are narrowed as the motion unfolds; attribute dropout does this in head 1
a₂ enters as a new action token at tₖ
run to tₖ, apply the new action to the predicted state, restart with the
clock at zero (predict_jobs takes a start state); an action starting at tₖ
inside one rollout needs the motion pilot's timed-intervention data
P edited, or an object dropped from S
edit the property numbers or drop an object, run again; attribute sweeps
and removals are training inputs; with head 2 the answer gets a spread
S scene table P properties a action s₀ start state sᴛ end state. Blue: given and clamped. Amber: generated.
